body:
## Summary
- Add the CR-204A public preparation adapter: idempotent Sonar child dispatch via inbox keys, dispatch outbox/inbox reconciliation, worker leases, child evidence aggregation, retry/terminal fan-out, and linked-order advancement.
- Extend shared preparation store (memory + Postgres) with child job refs, terminal failure, order lookup, and retry-wait wake helpers used by the adapter.
- Wire `CollectionReportOrchestrator` / `OrderOrchestrator` to drive linked shared preparation work while collection-report orders are producing.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run src/__tests__/public-preparation-adapter.test.ts` (13/13)
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run src/__tests__/shared-preparation-store.test.ts` (16/16)
- [ ] Production Sonar port wiring + HTTP worker bootstrap (follow-up; fixture port only in this PR)
- [ ] Postgres integration run against migrated schema

## Coordinator
- Bead: `collection-report-coordinator-f09.30`
- Sprint: CR-204A acceptance in `grimoires/loa/sprint.md`

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

## Findings

<!-- bridge-findings-start -->
```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "CR204A-001",
      "title": "Idempotency redelivery test does not advance harness clock",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "testing",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/__tests__/public-preparation-adapter.test.ts:148",
      "description": "expireLease({ value: now }) mutates a throwaway object; the harness clock is `let now` closed over by makeHarness(() => now). After the first processWork, the second call still observes now=2000 while PUBLIC_PREP_WORKER_LEASE_MS is 30000, so acquireLease returns busy and the assertion that dispatchCalls did not grow can pass without exercising reclaim/redelivery idempotency.",
      "suggestion": "Advance the real clock (e.g. now += 31_000, or expireLease(h.clock) when using makeHarness()'s clock object) before the second processWork, and assert the second call actually re-enters dispatch/probe rather than returning busy.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-002",
      "title": "All Sonar ingredient jobs share one idempotency key per order",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "correctness",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:66",
      "description": "prepIngredientJobs maps every work item to idempotency_key: ingredientJobIdempotencyKey(orderId, \"sonar\"). Multi-deployment work (covered by the staged-expansion test with 2 items) therefore projects distinct child jobs under a single key, which collapses or races kitchen/enqueue dedupe for all but one deployment.",
      "suggestion": "Key idempotency per work item or deployment (e.g. include work_item_id or deployment digest in ingredientJobIdempotencyKey), and assert distinct keys in the multi-deployment test.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-003",
      "title": "Active execution capacity acquired on prepare path is not released on ready",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "category": "resource-lifecycle",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:175",
      "description": "processWork optionally acquireActiveExecutionLease for the first linked order while preparing, and failLinkedOrders releases capacity on terminal_failure, but advanceLinkedOrders / finalize-ready success paths never release. Shared prep that reaches ready can leave collection_prep pool leases held until some unrelated path releases them.",
      "suggestion": "Release (or convert) the execution lease when work becomes ready, on retry_wait if the lease should not span waits, and ensure acquire failures are handled rather than ignored.",
      "confidence": 0.78
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-004",
      "title": "Reconcile path can abort entire worker tick on fencing errors",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "reliability",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:108",
      "description": "tick() calls reconcileLostDispatches without a SharedPreparationFencingError guard, then only catches fencing inside the listLeasableWork loop. Reconciliation calls recordChildJobRef with the current lease_epoch while holding no lease; a concurrent worker that bumped the epoch causes fencing to throw and skip all subsequent wake/process work for that tick.",
      "suggestion": "Catch SharedPreparationFencingError per pending row in reconcileLostDispatches (or around the reconcile call in tick), and optionally require a lease before mutating child refs.",
      "confidence": 0.88
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-005",
      "title": "Postgres recordChildJobRef conflates not-found/wrong-state with fencing",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "consistency",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/shared-preparation-store-postgres.ts:787",
      "description": "When the UPDATE returns no rows, Postgres always throws SharedPreparationFencingError. InMemory distinguishes missing item/parent (StateError), wrong parent state (StateError), and stale epoch (FencingError). Callers that treat fencing as skippable can silently ignore durable data bugs or wrong-state updates.",
      "suggestion": "Match in-memory semantics: SELECT parent/item first (or use distinct SQL branches) and throw StateError vs FencingError appropriately.",
      "confidence": 0.92
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-006",
      "title": "PublicPreparationWorker allows overlapping ticks",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-worker.ts:14",
      "description": "start() fires void this.tick() on an interval with no in-flight guard. If adapter.tick() exceeds publicPrepWorkerIntervalMs (default 5s), concurrent ticks can interleave lease acquire, dispatch intent, and reconciliation on the same work.",
      "suggestion": "Add a single-flight lock (ignore/schedule next run while one tick is active) or use a recursive setTimeout that schedules only after await completes.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-007",
      "title": "Dispatch ledger is in-memory only",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "durability",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-dispatch-store.ts:1",
      "description": "PublicPrepDispatchStore has only InMemoryPublicPrepDispatchStore, while SharedPreparationStore has a Postgres implementation. Lost-response reconciliation and intent/ack correlation therefore do not survive process restart in any Postgres-backed deployment path wired like the shared prep store.",
      "suggestion": "Add a Postgres-backed dispatch ledger (or document CR-204A as fixture-only and keep the worker/adapter behind an explicit non-prod gate until the store exists).",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-008",
      "title": "Child evidence aggregation uses stale item list and single deployment",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "correctness",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:198",
      "description": "On indexed probe, buildEvidence?.(work, items) passes the pre-loop items snapshot, and the default path aggregates only [item.deployment_id]. Parent finalize later aggregates all afterItems deployment ids. If publishChildEvidence validates coverage/freshness against full work-key policy, per-child publish can under-cover or disagree with finalize evidence.",
      "suggestion": "Build child evidence from the refreshed work item (and the policy’s expected coverage for that child), and keep parent aggregate on the full ready set; add a test that publish + finalize evidence stay consistent for multi-deployment work.",
      "confidence": 0.7
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-009",
      "title": "Fixture readiness digests are constant across all work",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "correctness",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-evidence.ts:44",
      "description": "buildReadinessEvidenceFromDeployments hashes fixed seeds \"prep-source\" / \"prep-evidence\", so source_digest and evidence_digest are identical for every work regardless of deployment_coverage. Any qualification or dedupe that trusts those digests cannot distinguish collections.",
      "suggestion": "Derive digest inputs from sorted deployment digests, generation, and policy/adapter versions (even for fixtures), and keep freshness/qualification honest to observed probe time.",
      "confidence": 0.72
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-010",
      "title": "Capacity acquire result ignored; only first subscriber charged",
      "severity": "MEDIUM",
      "category": "correctness",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:168",
      "description": "When capacityStore is set, acquireActiveExecutionLease is awaited without checking denial/busy, and only links[0] is used. Prep continues under admission pressure, and multi-subscriber fan-in capacity accounting is tied to an arbitrary first link.",
      "suggestion": "Handle non-acquired results (retry_wait or idle), and define explicit pool accounting for shared work (one prep lease per work_id, not per first order) in the store API.",
      "confidence": 0.68
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-011",
      "title": "syncSubscriberAttention(terminal=true) is a no-op",
      "severity": "LOW",
      "category": "dead-code",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:410",
      "description": "The loop does if (terminal) continue for every link, so failLinkedOrders’ await syncSubscriberAttention(work, code, true) never patches orders. Terminal attention relies solely on the failed transition; the terminal flag path is dead.",
      "suggestion": "Remove the terminal call, or implement a distinct terminal attention projection and drop the continue-all branch.",
      "confidence": 0.96
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-012",
      "title": "markLostResponse is unused by reconciliation selection",
      "severity": "LOW",
      "category": "api-design",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-dispatch-store.ts:82",
      "description": "listPendingReconciliation selects any unacked row older than 5s and never reads lost_response. markLostResponse only sets a flag that does not affect listing or replay priority.",
      "suggestion": "Either filter/prioritize lost_response=true in listPendingReconciliation, or remove the flag until a consumer exists.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-013",
      "title": "getActiveWorkForOrder returns terminal/ready work without state filter",
      "severity": "LOW",
      "category": "correctness",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/shared-preparation-store-postgres.ts:880",
      "description": "Both in-memory and Postgres return the latest non-detached link’s work regardless of state. CollectionReportOrchestrator will keep calling processWork for ready/failed work on every producing poll, re-running advance/fail fanout.",
      "suggestion": "Filter to active prep states for the orchestrator hot path, or make processWork short-circuit without re-patching when subscriber projection is already applied.",
      "confidence": 0.74
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-014",
      "title": "Lease fencing and inbox idempotency are structured correctly",
      "severity": "PRAISE",
      "category": "design",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:250",
      "description": "Dispatch records intent before Sonar calls, keys commands by generation×deployment×capability×adapter, and reconciles unacked intents by replaying the same inbox key. Store methods take expected_lease_epoch and the adapter continues on fencing during processWork. This is a solid at-least-once dispatch design for shared prep.",
      "suggestion": "Keep this pattern when adding a durable dispatch store and tighten reconcile fencing handling so the rest of the tick still runs.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-015",
      "title": "Adapter tests cover outage, fan-in, multi-child ready, and orchestrator hook",
      "severity": "PRAISE",
      "category": "testing",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/__tests__/public-preparation-adapter.test.ts:1",
      "description": "The suite exercises admission-before-dispatch, Sonar outage → retry_wait → wake, contested lease reclaim at the store, reject-policy multi-child readiness, subscriber fan-out on ready/fail, and CollectionReportOrchestrator invoking processWork. That matches the CR-204A behavioral surface well.",
      "suggestion": "Fix the expireLease clock bug and add coverage for capacity release on ready and Postgres dispatch/error-parity once those stores exist.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "id": "CR204A-016",
      "title": "Linked orders not yet in producing are skipped on terminal prep failure",
      "severity": "SPECULATION",
      "category": "lifecycle",
      "file": "packages/services/ordering/src/public-preparation-adapter.ts:372",
      "description": "failLinkedOrders only transitions orders with state === \"producing\". Late joiners or orders still in placed/routing when shared work fails remain linked to failed work without refusal projection until something else moves them.",
      "suggestion": "Confirm product rules for non-producing subscribers; if they should fail or detach, handle those states explicitly in failLinkedOrders.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    }
  ]
}
```
